newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU monetary committee meets on single currency.
newsitem.headline: EU monetary committee meets on single currency.

text.p: The European Union's monetary committee began a two-day meeting on Monday to discuss a budget stability pact for countries joining a future economic and monetary union (EMU).
No information was immediately available from the meeting, with many of the members remaining tight-lipped after the first day ended.
The group, comprising national treasury and central bank officials, was also due to focus on a post-EMU exchange rate grid, linking the single currency to those not in the core group.

In addition, a discussion was expected on the legal framework for the single currency, an issue of particular relevance to those worried about the continuity of financial contracts after the EMU's expected launch in 1999.
The decisions reached by the monetary committee will be forwarded to an informal meeting of EU finance ministers and central bankers in Dublin on September 21.
The committee will resume its work on Tuesday morning.
